question: What distinguishes method overloading from method overriding in Java?
options: They are the same concept with different names
Overloading only works with static methods
Overriding happens within a single class, while overloading requires inheritance
Overloading defines multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists in the same class, while overriding redefines an inherited method in a subclass
explanation: Overloading is having multiple methods with the same name but different parameters within one class; overriding is a subclass providing a new implementation for an inherited method with the same signature.
